- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true mean over 3–5 days, apply a 2–3% upward bias to reflect mean reversion toward higher levels.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast volatility by smoothing the last 3–5 points to avoid overreaction to noise.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, assume momentum bias and increase next forecast by 1–3% to capture continuation.  
- If sentiment is low but true outcome is rising, assume delayed reaction — delay forecast adjustment until sentiment turns positive.
